introHtml:
Marketing directors, HR directors, safety managers, and business owners: finding the right custom t-shirts for your next event, team, or promotion can be overwhelming. You need shirts that fit well, feel great, and represent your brand or message clearly. Whether you're outfitting a safety crew, launching a new product, or building team spirit for a charity walk, the right t-shirt makes a lasting impression. At Perfect Imprints, we offer a wide selection of styles from trusted brands like Gildan, Hanes, District, and Port & Company, so you can find the perfect base for your design.

Our catalog includes classic crewnecks, tri-blend tees, ladies' fits, youth sizes, and even camo options for specialized needs. With decoration methods like screen printing, embroidery, and full-color heat transfer, we can bring your logo or artwork to life on virtually any color shirt. Bulk orders are our specialty, and we help you navigate minimum quantities and pricing to stay within budget. From 50 shirts for a small business team to 5,000 for a national event, we deliver quality custom apparel that your people will actually want to wear.
buyingGuideHtml:
Custom T-Shirts Buying Guide

When ordering custom t-shirts, start with the fabric and fit. Cotton tees are breathable and budget-friendly, while tri-blend fabrics (cotton, polyester, rayon) offer a softer, more modern feel. For safety managers, consider high-visibility colors or moisture-wicking blends for outdoor crews. Always order a size sample before placing a bulk run, especially if you're mixing men's, women's, and youth sizes. Fit varies by brand, so test a few styles like the Gildan Softstyle or District Perfect Tri Tee to see what your team prefers.

Decoration method matters. Screen printing is cost-effective for large runs with simple logos, while embroidery adds a premium look for polo-style shirts. Full-color heat transfer works well for complex designs with gradients or photos. For smaller quantities, direct-to-garment (DTG) printing is an option but typically has higher per-unit costs. Discuss your artwork with your account manager to choose the method that balances quality and budget for your promotional t-shirts.

Use cases vary widely. Marketing directors often order branded t-shirts for trade shows, product launches, or customer appreciation gifts. HR directors use them for employee onboarding swag or company picnic uniforms. Safety managers need durable, high-visibility tees for field crews, often with reflective stripes or safety slogans. Business owners might order custom t-shirts for a local fundraiser, a sports team sponsorship, or a small retail line. The right shirt can reinforce your brand every time it's worn.

Bulk orders typically start at 24 to 48 pieces for screen printing, but some decoration methods like embroidery may have lower minimums. As quantity increases, per-unit price drops significantly. For example, ordering 500 custom t-shirts instead of 100 can cut your cost per shirt by 30% or more. If you're planning a recurring event, consider ordering extra stock to cover future needs. Wholesale t-shirt pricing is available for orders over 144 pieces, making it easier to stay within budget for large campaigns.

Common buying mistakes include ignoring shrinkage. Pre-shrunk cotton is standard, but tri-blends and polyesters hold their shape better. Also, don't assume all sizes fit the same: a women's cut tee from one brand may fit differently than another. Always request a sample pack that includes your top three style choices in the sizes you'll order most. Finally, factor in production time. Screen printing typically takes 7-10 business days, while embroidery or heat transfer may be faster. Plan ahead, especially for seasonal events or tight deadlines.

For the best results, provide high-resolution artwork (vector files preferred) and specify exact placement and size. Your account manager can guide you through the setup process and recommend decoration methods based on your design and budget. Whether you need 50 or 5,000, Perfect Imprints delivers consistent quality on every order.

faqs.q: What is the minimum order quantity for custom t-shirts?
faqs.a: Minimum order quantities vary by decoration method. Screen printing typically requires 24-48 pieces, while embroidery may have a lower minimum of 12. Full-color heat transfer can sometimes be done in smaller runs. Contact us for specific MOQs based on your design and shirt choice.

faqs.q: Which t-shirt fabric is best for screen printing?
faqs.a: 100% cotton or high-cotton blends work best for screen printing because the fibers hold ink well. Tri-blends and polyesters can also be printed but may require special inks or pretreatment. Discuss your fabric choice with your account manager to ensure the best print quality.

faqs.q: Can I get a sample before placing a bulk order?
faqs.a: Yes, we recommend ordering a sample of your chosen shirt style and size to check fit, color, and feel. Samples can be ordered as single pieces. We also offer printed samples for an additional fee to approve artwork placement and color before full production.

faqs.q: How long does production take for custom t-shirts?
faqs.a: Typical production time is 7-10 business days for screen printing after artwork approval. Embroidery and heat transfer may be faster, around 5-7 business days. Rush orders are available for an additional fee. Always confirm lead times with your account manager before placing an order.

faqs.q: What file format do you need for artwork?
faqs.a: We prefer vector files such as Adobe Illustrator (.ai), .eps, or .pdf for best results. High-resolution raster files like .tiff or .png at 300 DPI are also acceptable. If you only have a low-resolution image, we can sometimes recreate it, but at an additional cost.
